comments.value:
Wait, are private worlds being visible in the website?
If so, that should be reported as that should not be happening at all.
If it's in relation to the launch codes specifically, it works from anywhere not just the website, i personally use those to connect to private worlds my friends allowed me to connect and use as a "hub" per se.
Just trying to understand what this is really about.

@{5c1d0571e2b306156fd044e3|full_name}: It's a slight change to the website to stop people from creating links to other people's private world's without their permission, this is to make it so the owner is the only one that sees the create link button.

@{5be5de3fed2e2c2c89b4415f|full_name}: That is really odd, i've never heard of that happening before, and it shouldn't be happening either.
In terms of launch codes, the only way to connect to a private world is via knowing the ID of the world, as far as i'm aware there is no other way of doing such, unless they're exploiting something.
And the only way to get a world ID (legitimately atleast) is by connecting to said private world to begin with, which they'd need to go through the owner first.

@{5c1d0571e2b306156fd044e3|full_name}: well if say the owner creates a friend+ version of their private world and then a bunch of people join, they can then go to the website and create their own launch codes.

@{5be5de3fed2e2c2c89b4415f|full_name}: With all due respect, why would the map owner make a friends+ instance of their own world when they want it to be private to begin with?
The concept of the more the merrier aside, it really doesn't make all that much sense to do so when you want the world to be exclusively private based on the context we're going for, as a simple friends only or invite+ would do just fine and keep any unwanted visitors away.
I understand where you're coming from with it, and creators should have more control over who can or cannot join their private worlds, but i don't see removing the launching code functionality as the appropriate measure here, alot of people such as myself do use such extensively, and this wouldn't really harm anybody that exploits the system, as they will find a way to do so anyway.

@{5c1d0571e2b306156fd044e3|full_name}: I just think it sounds like a good idea for the map owner to have the control on who has access to the map, this post is only regarding private world's, public world functionality on the website would stay the same.

If someone wished to have a link to the map they should have to ask the owner.

Besides private maps are maps that have not yet been approved for public usage by the VRChat team, and the owner should have sole responsibility on who accesses them.

@{5be5de3fed2e2c2c89b4415f|full_name}: It's not based upon functionality on the website, i'm talking about the launch code as a whole, as i've stated prior, i use a launch code to connect to a private world owned by a friend, without that functionality i can't access my friends' world without them being present.
You don't generate a code based solely on the website, it's how vrchat handles connections all around, what i'm trying to get at here is that this won't simply allow world owners the complete control over who can and cannot access their private worlds, even if they gave consent prior, nobody will be able to connect to their worlds anymore unless they're explicitly present, and i can bet that any portal that links to a private world uses the same functionality.
So we'll be scraping a base functionality that is not talked about much but has quite alot of potential to allow world owners the possiblity of allowing other users to connect to their worlds, we do not have any system in place that allows friends to connect to our private worlds as far as i'm aware.
TL;DR : This will remove a standard function that's barely talked about, on the basis of people that once joined your world being able to do so again without your direct consent.

@{5c1d0571e2b306156fd044e3|full_name}: I don't think your understanding this correctly the functionality for creating links is not being removed, the page is being modified to have the owner be the person that creates them (only on private world's).

A link that your friend makes you will still work fine.

@{5be5de3fed2e2c2c89b4415f|full_name}: I feel like we're both misunderstanding something then.
People don't really... "make" links, the launch codes are essentially static, the world ID is the only thing taken into general account and then it has some flags attached to the command to dictate if it's private or not (the instance that is not the world), people shouldn't be able to connect to worlds that are private through the website, like, at all.
What is being asked here, as stated by yui "i suggest making the launch option for private maps only available to the map creator" which means scrapping the direct connections made by the Launch Code, not the links generated by the website.
Correct me if i'm wrong, i'm prone to confusing things.

@{5c1d0571e2b306156fd044e3|full_name}: Yes, "people shouldn't be able to connect to worlds that are private through the website" (unless your the owner) is the issue this post is addressing.  

I don't believe they would change the functionality of the IDs, but if they wished to do that at the same time to allow more granular control, I am fine with that too.

@{5be5de3fed2e2c2c89b4415f|full_name}: If the issue is indeed the case of people connecting to worlds via the website that they never had gone to before, without the owners' consent, then i'm all on board.
If on the other hand it's in regards to removing launch functionalities like i mentioned prior, not so much.
Guess i'll wait on yui to confirm which is the case, as the wording is rather vague.
@{5c1d0571e2b306156fd044e3|full_name}: if you have the world ID you can directly look it up on the website and launch your own instance
@{5a2ab16cfc55d1544366d654|full_name}: So it's on the basis of the launch codes, since it again, relies on the user knowing the world ID to even do such.
@{5c1d0571e2b306156fd044e3|full_name}: you can get the world id to any world with the output log anyway
@{5c1d0571e2b306156fd044e3|full_name}: so if they could just disable creating your own private instance on the website it would make it more difficult for something such as this to happen

@{5a2ab16cfc55d1544366d654|full_name}: Of course you can, that's how you get it to begin with, the thing is, it requires the user to firsthand have first accessed the world to even do such.
So in a nutshell, this is calling for the removal of the direct connections on the basis of launch codes in regards to private worlds, correct?
@{5c1d0571e2b306156fd044e3|full_name}: its to make is so only the world owner can launch an instance of their own private world from the website

@{5a2ab16cfc55d1544366d654|full_name}: But the thing is, doing such will alter how launching works as a whole, as connections are made the same exact way.
So i personally don't support such as it's yet another roadblock, both launch codes and the website deals with connections the same exact way, making it impossible for users, again, to connect to private worlds made by friends unless they're explicitly present.
@{5c1d0571e2b306156fd044e3|full_name}: no it wont, you just make it unavailable through only the website, i believe you are misunderstanding my greatly.

@{5c1d0571e2b306156fd044e3|full_name}: all you gotta do it remove the option for other users. thats all... it shouldnt interfere with anyone launching on their own account or how launching works in general, it will just check if the world owner is the one who is trying to launch or enter that page, and if not it will not show the option to

@{5a2ab16cfc55d1544366d654|full_name}: I'm sorry if that's the case, and if it is, please enlighten me on how they differ, i've worked with launch codes extenssively and mostly know how they function altogether, and i'm not trying to be hostile or condescending in any way, and i apologize if it may seem that way.
But it honestly just seems like it will lead to such.

My only issue regarding the topic is the fact that private worlds won't be accessible via launch commands as the website deals with them the same way, and as such, not allowing it on one side will disallow it on the other, so i'm personally not up for it at all.

@{5c1d0571e2b306156fd044e3|full_name}: ok, well there are worlds that people want 100% private being passed around, this is an issue ive heard many many complaints about, they could make it a locally hosted world that only you can join via launch codes but cannot invite anyone due to privacy reasons, though im not entirely confident that would happen. The big issue is things that are supposed to be private are no longer private.
@{5c1d0571e2b306156fd044e3|full_name}: I think they're saying, for private worlds, to hide the "new instance" button from everyone except for the owner.

@{5c8087a771f44410953098eb|full_name}:
In terms of the client : (http://prntscr.com/mudq0t) such is impossible (legimately atleast), and i still think the same should be applied to the website, but as it stands, and i've checked, they provide a launch code (http://prntscr.com/muds9r), which is the identical launch code for literally every other world with a different tag depending on what it wants to do (instance number, session type, etc) it doesn't have a button to create a new instance but will infact give you a direct launch code.
I'm completely fine with the idea of not allowing users to generate new instances based on the website, but if it does infact alter how private world instances are handled, as i've stated before, i'm agaisn't such.
And i reiterate once more, i'm completely up to support having the same "restrictions" in terms of what we have on the client, but based on how worlds are connected to through the website (generating launch codes) that won't be the only thing altered, and restrictions will most likely apply.
Call me cynical, but i've seen this happen time and time again.
This wouldn't work, because, you can make a link to any world, all you need is the world ID. I could just make an instance of any world and change the world ID of it.

They can try limit this a bit, but after all you just need that world id and you can create URL manually, so to any world you visited at least once. (or even just seen one of your friends in it)

They would need to create whole system to limit creation of instances to owner only for private worlds.
There is more then one website out there that lists none public or even deleted worlds. https://en.vrcw.net/world?keyword=Hagbard+Celine

I think is is closer to being a bug than a feature request.

There is a bug report about this, here: https://feedback.vrchat.com/bug-reports/p/access-to-private-worlds

But there is a bit of an issue in how private worlds are handled nowadays it seems. The current behavior is better described as "Unlisted" rather than "Private".

I would love it if it was possible to select rather a world is just unlisted, or actually private and only usable with the world author.

details: Ive noticed a few people launching private worlds that people want to keep private from the website, i suggest making the launch option for private maps only available to the map creator
title: Make private worlds unable to launch on the website from anyone but the owner
